recipes.name: Drunken Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds large shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 tablespoon red pepper flakes, or to taste

steps.text: Heat canola oil in a large skillet over high heat. Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook and stir until just fragrant, about 15 seconds. Add shrimp, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes; cook and stir until shrimp is slightly pink, about 2 to 4 minutes. Stir in beer, ketchup, and sugar; bring sauce to a boil.

Dissolve cornstarch in water, and stir into boiling sauce. Cook until the sauce returns to a boil and thickens, the shrimp are bright pink on the outside, and no longer transparent in the center, about 2 minutes more. Stir in sesame oil; remove from heat. Sprinkle with green onions and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Drunken Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: This drunken shrimp dish features large succulent shrimp stir-fried with onion, garlic, and fresh ginger in a sweet and spicy beer-based sauce.

review.reviewBody:
For this recipe; I took the reviews into consideration and mixed up the sequence for awesome, fabulous results!

Mixed beer, ketchup, sugar, red pepper (little less because I ran out) and cornstarch (sans TBLS of water) until well blended. Sautéd onions and garlic in sesame oil. Added beer/ketchup mix and it instantly thickened! That was a surprise! Reduced heat and added shrimp until cooked through. Topped with green onions. Sauce was thick and flavorful and the shrimp cooked perfectly. I wonder if my results were because I did in a cast iron pan? This was amazing and we served with pasta. Would make for an awesome appetizer! Will repeat for many weeknights or get-togethers in the future!! Thank you!!

Loved it, I made the sauce first like was on other reviews because I used shrimp left over from shrimp cocktail. I think next time I would double the sauce so there was extra for the rice. It was really spicy, should the red pepper be 1 tsp int 1 tbl? I think I will try on chicken...
I’ve made drunken shrimp many times, but this recipe with the added sesame oil and fresh ginger is our favorite

I would definitely make this again. My husband and I both loved it. I added more ginger and more garlic, and I followed folks suggestions to add the shrmp later. They came out perfectly cooked. I served it over egg noodles.

The main change I made was using a piece of frozen ginger (that's how I keep it) and my microplane. You don't need to peel it -- the skin disappears when you shred it like that. Then the flavor is more evenly distributed. I also use peanut oil. Next time, I'll skip the sugar. I think it was more than sweet enough. Or maybe a splash of mirin.

SOOOO yummy and spicey. My husband hates spicey food but he could not stop eating these, I've made the recipe 3 times always turns out great, I didn't have fresh ginger but used the dry one and it was just fine

I read the reviews and made those changes that sounded doable for Mr. Picky. Used one pound of shrimp and doubled the sauce. I skipped the red pepper flakes and substituted a tablespoon of fresh lemon juice instead. Used tomato sauce instead of ketchup. Cut the sugar back to 1/2 tbsp and added a few sprinkles of Italian Seasoning and served over linguini with the green onions and some freshly grated parmesan cheese Made the sauce and taste tested before I added the shrimp. The result was a mild, tasty dish, suitable for anyone who might have an issue with spicy foods. Delicious served with garden fresh green beans, warm buttered French bread, and watermelon. Had enough leftovers for another two servings. Will make again. Yum! Thank you.

We really liked this dish. I didn't read the reviews ahead of time, and I should have made the sauce first and cooked it down some before I added the shrimp, so they were a bit overdone. No points off for that, though, because they were still very tasty and the leftovers were still amazing. I added less than a teaspoon of red pepper flakes. Gave it a nice, mild zing. I could have added more, but a whole tablespoon would have been way too much. Next time I might finish it off with a squeeze of lemon or lime juice, but it was great as is, too. Served it with some crusty garlic bread and a garden salad. Yum!
We really enjoyed this recipe! I made as directed, except I used 1 pound of medium shrimp and I waited and added the shrimp to the sauce, and let it cook in the sauce. Thank you for sharing!!

Very spicy!! I only added 1 tsp of red pepper flakes and next time I’ll do half. I listened to the other reviews and made the sauce first and added shrimp last. We served it over brown rice and enjoyed it!
I think everyone in here complaining about “rubbery shrimp” is using precooked. Buy raw!
Nicely balanced flavors, and my picky husband liked! I followed the instructions exactly.
I added Pappardelle!!!
I substituted red wine for the beer and 6 oz tomato paste instead of ketchup, cornstarch, and sugar. I served it over fusilli pasta and it was amazing!

Great easy recipe, but I thought i could handle heat, but either I screwed up the time and cook the red pepper flakes too long or something else. It was really hot but had a great taste before the heat hit. Sms
Made exactly as written and served over cold soba noodles with a sesame/soy dressing and beer. So good!

Oh my goodness.! My mouth is still on fire in a good way!!! Based on other reviews, I cut the sugar in 1/2 and backed off the red chili flakes. WHEN I make it again, I'll use 1/4-1/2 on the red chili flakes and let my husband doctor his own. Great flavors and will definitely make if again!
My son, who likes spicy food, even said a bit too much heat. Like other comments would cut the red better if I try it again.
Not very flavorful.
Family loved it. I made no changes. I served it over rice.
